text: Two airline pilots spotted something impossible at sixteen thousand feet.
A man. Sitting in a lawn chair.
In 1982, Larry Walters tied forty-two helium balloons to a chair in his California backyard.
Instead, he shot nearly three miles into the sky.
He'd brought a pellet gun to pop balloons and come back down.
But after shooting a few, he dropped the gun.
As the chair descended, he dumped water ballast to control his landing.
Then his ropes snagged power lines.
The FAA fined him fifteen hundred dollars.
That same lawn chair is now in the Smithsonian.
